summary: The Dashboard, the page every return opens on, now says where you stand and what to do next, in plain words, above the four figures the owner chose.
points: It opens with 'Hi Ana.' and one plain sentence, like 'Your month works. Building your cushion for surprises is next.'

Three lines show what is left over each month, how many months the cushion covers and whether retirement is on track, each with a coloured dot and a few words. Tapping a line opens the page behind it.
The page's one filled button is your next move ('Your next move: Keep one month of bills in cash').
After Set up my plan, the old checklist folds to 'Set up your plan: done' instead of pointing the button at 'Check the assumptions'.
Big figures stay on one line: '$572,700' no longer breaks into '$572,' and '700'.
An empty Dashboard starts with Set up my plan: 'Do steps 1 to 5 in one go'.
numbers: Ranked first of 31 findings from a nine-agent phone walk-through
4 households checked on a phone, in dark mode and on a desktop

shots.caption: Before: four tiles with split figures, generic cards, nothing about where you stand.
After: 'Hi Ana.', the plain sentence, three status lines and your next move, then the tiles on one line.
An empty plan starts with Set up my plan.
